description_text: COMPANY DESCRIPTION The company’s objective is to enhance the efficiency of municipal and industrial wastewater treatment plants. Hence it is confronted with various issues related to biological and chemical processes regarding the treatment of wastewater. PROBLEM DESCRIPTION The sedimentation of small suspended or colloidal solid particles (especially organic substances) is an essential process in various stages of wastewater treatment. These particles are bound together to form larger 'flocs'. These 'flocs' settle much faster due to their mass, which makes the process more efficient. Artificial polymer flocculants are used to create these 'flocs'. The consumption of flocculants during the dewatering of digested sludge often varies significantly, as digested sludge contains large amounts of capillary and cell water. Some causes are well-known for this phenomenon, such as the fact that certain microorganisms die during the digestion process, releasing cell wall residues that form colloids, which also bind water, or the re-dissolution of phosphates, which can also bind significant amounts of water. As a result, mechanical dewatering methods (e.g. centrifuges, diverse presses) reach their limitations in effectively processing the sludge. Despite the use of flocculants, a considerable proportion of bound water remains in the sludge, which limits the achievable dry matter content. Precise process control, optimised flocculant dosing, and potentially pre-treatment measures such as the use of dewatering aids or sludge conditioning can help mitigate these challenges. Therefore, the amount of flocculants used should be minimised for cost reasons without negatively influencing the sedimentation process. In fact, a suitable flocculation process ensures that the proportion of bound water can be minimised and the achievable dry matter content can be optimised. This is of interest as a high water content increases the costs for further treatment of the digested sludge (e.g. incineration). STATE OF THE ART Currently, many of the factors limiting the effectiveness of flocculation processes remain unknown. Flocculants do not always work equally well, even though they are used in the same wastewater treatment plant. In addition to the well-known charge changes between summer and winter sludge, there are also significant fluctuations in polymer consumption that occur independently of seasonal variations. The reasons for this are not yet sufficiently understood. Whenever flocculant consumption increases or the dry matter content of the dewatered sludge decreases, immediate action is required. In practice, fresh samples of digested sludge are taken from the wastewater treatment plants and flocculation trials are conducted in the laboratory. The flocculants identified during these trials are subsequently tested in pilot-scale experiments and then used in the wastewater treatment plant for as long as the performance meets the expectations of the plant operator. Once the efficiency of the process decreases, new samples are collected and additional tests are carried out to identify the appropriate flocculants. These tests are both time-consuming and cost-intensive for flocculant suppliers and plant operators alike. The goal is to understand the causes of fluctuations, improve the efficiency of sludge dewatering, reduce resource consumption, and simultaneously minimise operating costs and time required for trials and adjustments. The emphasis should remain on fostering sustainable and innovative development throughout the process. PARTNER SOUGHT The Austrian company is interested in a commercial agreement with technical assistance as well as in joint development projects.
technical_problem_evidence_text: The company is seeking expertise in process optimisation and associated technologies (e.g. sensors, equipment) that enable the cost-efficient and effective use of flocculants in municipal and industrial wastewater treatment plants. Suppliers of novel and innovative flocculants are also welcome. Particular interest lies in solutions and expertise that contribute to reducing the water content of digested sludge and improving sludge dewatering performance. Expertise in the following areas is particularly desirable: - causes of fluctuations occurring with flocculants - process control - optimised flocculant dosing - pre-treatment measures such as the use of dewatering aids or sludge conditioning - efficiency of sludge dewatering - general reduction in resource consumption - …
title: Austrian company is looking for expertise for reducing flocculants and water content in wastewater treatment plants

description_text: The Austrian SME, founded in 2012, develops innovative technologies for surface functionalization, with a particular focus on the metallization of technical substrates. Together with their partners, they can draw on many years of experience in plasma technology, systems engineering and production automation. A key area of application is the functionalization of aluminum surfaces to make them suitable for subsequent soldering processes, such as those used in the electronics and printed circuit board industries. This makes it possible to replace the conventionally used copper with aluminum, which is cheaper and much lighter. The Austrian company already has established market access to the electronics industry and specifically targets applications in the fields of printed circuit boards, electronic assemblies, and innovative connection technologies. As part of the further development of this technology, the SME is now seeking industrial partners with experience in etching aluminum structures, such as those typically found in printed circuit boards and electronic assemblies.
technical_problem_evidence_text: Potential partners could include, for example: •    manufacturers of chemicals for aluminum etching •    chemical processors or process service providers for aluminum etching •    equipment manufacturers with expertise in etching and inline processing Ideally, partners should come from the following fields: •    etching of formed parts, •    spray etching of fine metal structures, •    or continuous inline etching processes for metallic materials. The Austrian SME is looking for partners who: •    can provide suitable etching chemicals and process chemicals, •    possess in-depth expertise in etching processes and integration into industrial manufacturing processes, •    actively support joint technological development, •    and are interested in the subsequent joint marketing of the technology in the printed circuit board and electronics markets. Of particular importance is a process chemistry that can be implemented as simply, reliably, and cost-effectively as possible on existing etching lines in the electronics industry or on lines modified with minimal effort.
title: Austrian SME is seeking industrial partners in the field of aluminum etching

description_text: An Austrian company operating in the field of sustainable timber construction is developing next-generation building systems based on prefabricated timber panels. To further improve the environmental performance, circularity and adaptability of its construction solutions, the company is seeking an innovative connection technology for joining structural timber elements. Current fastening and connection solutions often require compromises between structural performance, ease of assembly, material health and circularity. The company is therefore looking for a novel connection concept that can simultaneously address these requirements while remaining suitable for industrial production and large-scale construction applications. The requested technology should enable the connection of timber wall, roof and floor elements in load-bearing applications. The solution should support modern industrial prefabrication processes and facilitate efficient on-site assembly, maintenance and future building modifications. The company is particularly interested in technologies that support circular construction principles through reversible and non-destructive disassembly, enabling multiple use cycles and preserving the value of building components and materials throughout their lifecycle. Potential cooperation may involve adaptation of an existing technology, co-development of a new connection system, testing and validation activities, material optimisation or industrial implementation. The company is open to commercial agreements with technical assistance as well as research and development cooperation agreements.
technical_problem_evidence_text: The company seeks a future-proof connection system designed according to open-building and circular-construction principles, ensuring long-term adaptability, interoperability and material innovation readiness. The sought technology should fulfil the following functional requirements: •	Suitable for structural timber construction applications. •	Enables connections between wall, roof and floor elements. •	Capable of transferring vertical, horizontal and dynamic loads. •	High mechanical strength and long-term durability. •	Suitable for repeated assembly and disassembly cycles. •	Compatible with industrial prefabrication processes. •	Facilitates rapid installation, maintenance and replacement. •	Supports future extensions, modifications and adaptive reuse of buildings. Material-related requirements include: •	Use of recyclable materials. •	Preference for PFAS-free solutions. •	Compliance with REACH regulations. •	Absence of substances of very high concern (SVHC). •	Efficient material use with low material intensity. •	High corrosion resistance. •	Long service life. •	Possibility to integrate bio-based materials or components. •	Low-emission materials supporting indoor air quality. •	Low VOC emissions and minimisation of hazardous substances. •	Consideration of human health criteria aligned with sustainability certification systems such as DGNB, Cradle-to-Cradle and LEED. Circular economy requirements include: •	Non-destructive disassembly. •	Multiple reuse cycles without significant performance loss. •	Easy separation of materials at end-of-life. •	Support for pure material streams and high-quality recycling. •	Preservation of material value throughout the lifecycle. •	Compatibility with cradle-to-cradle design principles. •	Potential integration into take-back systems. •	Facilitation of secondary markets and remanufacturing of building components. System-level requirements: •	Enable compatibility across multiple generations of building systems, from existing solutions (Generation 1) to future developments (Generation X). •	Ensure backward compatibility with previously deployed panel systems and connection concepts. •	Support standardized and interoperable interfaces to facilitate integration across different manufacturers, suppliers and construction systems. •	Enable modular extensions and upgrades throughout the building lifecycle. •	Allow integration of future material innovations, including emerging bio-based, recycled or advanced engineered materials. •	Accommodate different panel configurations, dimensions and assembly concepts without requiring fundamental redesign of the connection system. •	Support adaptable building designs and evolving construction requirements over time. •	Facilitate long-term system scalability while maintaining structural integrity and ease of assembly.
title: Austrian construction company seeks circular and demountable connection technology for load-bearing timber panel systems

description_text: The Austrian deep-tech startup (a university spin-off) builds on more than 25 years of expertise in electrolysers and fuel cells. The company specialises in developing and manufacturing cutting-edge Membrane Electrode Assembly (MEA) technology that powers the hydrogen economy. In line with its activities in the development and production of electrochemical energy components, the startup is looking for European partners with roll-to-roll manufacturing capacity. The company develops membrane electrode components used in anion exchange membrane water electrolysis and proton exchange membrane fuel cells. These components include catalyst-coated membranes, catalyst-coated substrates and membrane electrode assemblies. The company currently builds its processes at laboratory and pilot scale and has access to a roll-to-roll pilot line for process validation and medium-volume production. After this validation step, external manufacturing capacity will be needed for larger and more regular production volumes. The purpose of this partner search is therefore to assess the availability of suitable European manufacturing capacity, including which capabilities are available, what technical limitations apply, and how cooperation could be structured. The external manufacturing need is expected from 2028 onwards. The required technology is roll-to-roll slot-die coating and related downstream processing for thin functional catalyst layers on flexible and, where possible, porous substrates. The preferred partner should be able to support not only coating but also drying, web handling, lamination, cutting or stamping, integration of gasket or subgasket materials, quality control, documentation and packaging. The expected production capacity is up to around 5,000 m² per year, depending on product mix and successful process transfer. The company is seeking cooperation with European industrial partners that already operate suitable roll-to-roll coating or converting lines, ideally with experience in functional coatings, electrochemical components, membranes, catalyst inks, fuel cells, electrolysers, batteries, sensors, printed electronics or comparable thin-film products. The minimum useful coating width is 300 mm; a width up to 800 mm would be ideal. Detailed coating formulations, layer structures, product drawings, process windows and customer-related specifications are confidential and would only be shared under a non-disclosure agreement and after an initial technical fit assessment. Cooperation could start with capability discussions and non-confidential process mapping, continue with feasibility trials and pilot campaigns, and later move into recurring manufacturing. The preferred cooperation types are an outsourcing agreement, a supplier agreement and, where process transfer or adaptation is needed, a commercial agreement with technical assistance.
technical_problem_evidence_text: The partner should be a European company, contract manufacturer or coating specialist operating roll-to-roll slot-die coating and converting equipment. The partner should first provide a non-confidential overview of its available line widths, coating technologies, compatible substrates, drying and lamination options, quality control methods, typical campaign sizes, available capacity and experience with functional coatings.
title: Seeking roll-to-roll slot-die manufacturing capacity for electrochemical membrane electrode components

description_text: Brussels-based energy technology company providing modular first-life LFP BESS together with a proprietary EMS and cloud analytics platform. The solution combines an integrated battery-and-energy management architecture with continuous monitoring and digital-twin-based analytics to optimize performance, reliability, and lifetime. Up to February 2026, 80 MW of smart-controlled flexible assets and manages 150 MWh of battery storage capacity, reflecting strong growth and a rapidly expanding position in the flexibility and storage market were operated by the company. Research is a core pillar of their activities to stay aligned with state-of-the-art methods and to shape future products based on market needs and emerging technologies. They are active in European (e.g., Horizon) and national R&D projects and focus on State-of-X topics (SoC/SoH), lifetime and Remaining Useful Life modelling and advanced EMS control for more efficient multi-asset power flow. The SME also aims to co-develop forecasting and smart control capabilities, including weather-condition–based forecasting, household consumption mapping, and AI-based control to optimize multi-asset power flow more efficiently.

description_text: This Belgian chocolate manufacturer has a long history behind its today's production, with longstanding expertise and craftmanship in every stage of chocolate making. They produce high-quality fine chocolates for branded manufacturers and for private labels and have built their reputation and the collaboration with their clients on a blended mix of creativity, innovation and quality. This results in a variety of fillings, shapes, molds, decorations. While wishing to keep all these characteristics  - which combine traditional skills and modern techniques - to deliver excellent products, they are confronted with the increasing of the production costs. Among the others, costs linked to the cocoa.
technical_problem_evidence_text: In order to limit the impact of raw material prices, and notably cocoa, this Belgian company is actively looking for vegetable fat to be used as an alternative to cocoa in the filling of their large range of chocolates, chocolate bars, pralines, truffles etc. The vegetable fat alternative will be used in the filling of the chocolate pralines and has to guarantee the same density and easiness to work the product as for traditional pralines stuffed with cocoa. The cocoa would then be used only for the external coating. The vegetable fat alternative sought needs to: - be used directly in production, without melting step, - ideally come in 20kg (max 25kg) for proper handling - be easily combined with the coating, which can be of simple chocolate or eg a praline powdered or enrobed with nuts, fruits - easily embrace the shape, moulds selected for the production The filling with vegetable fat alternative must be : -	close the density of the pralines with a traditional cocoa filling -	FSSC 22000 certified: Guaranteed food safety and quality standards -	from sourced ingredients produced in Europe by suppliers located in Europe The potential partner must have track records in the manufacturing of the vegetable fat alternative sought
title: Looking for vegetable fat to be used as an alternative to cocoa in the manufacturing of a large range of chocolates, chocolate bars, pralines, truffles etc

description_text: The organisation is currently assessing the feasibility of using online sensors and continuous monitoring technologies for the compliance monitoring of treated wastewater discharged from wastewater treatment plants. The parameters of interest mainly include: - Total Suspended Solids (TSS) - Chemical Oxygen Demand (COD) - Total Organic Carbon (TOC) - Nitrates The objective is to evaluate whether online measurements could partially substitute or complement conventional laboratory analyses while maintaining regulatory reliability and compliance. They are particularly interested in: - Types of sensors and technologies currently in use; - Operational constraints and field experience (maintenance, cleaning, recalibration, fouling, sensor drift, robustness, etc.); - Methodologies used to demonstrate equivalence, correlation or regulatory acceptance compared with standard laboratory analyses; - Existing pilot projects, case studies or operational deployments; - Partnerships for technical exchanges, benchmarking activities or collaborative projects.
technical_problem_evidence_text: They are seeking contacts with organisations that have already developed or tested such solutions in operational environments.
title: Seeking partners and feedback on online sensor technologies for wastewater treatment plant effluent compliance monitoring.

description_text: A Bulgarian deep-tech SME with long-standing expertise in geospatial technologies, surveying and infrastructure monitoring has developed a protected software-led autonomous air-water inspection and mapping technology. The technology is designed to bridge the operational gap between above-water and underwater surveying by combining observations from both environments into a single georeferenced operational model. Potential applications include dams and hydraulic structures, ports and harbour infrastructure, bridges, underwater pipelines and cables, coastal erosion and sediment monitoring, marine environmental monitoring, and underwater cultural heritage documentation. The software architecture, data-processing environment and artificial intelligence perception layer have already been developed. The current stage focuses on integration with real underwater hardware and validation in operational missions. The company is seeking European technology and industrial partners capable of providing, adapting or integrating an open and customisable underwater robotic platform. Relevant capabilities include payload capacity, onboard electrical power and thermal management for edge computing, access to vehicle telemetry and raw sensor data, documented software interfaces, and integration of customer-selected navigation, sonar, bathymetric and environmental sensors. Cooperation may involve integration with an existing commercially available underwater vehicle, adaptation of a platform for customer-supplied onboard computing and sensing equipment, physical and electrical integration, prototype manufacturing, laboratory and field testing, pilot validation and preparation for commercial deployment. The Bulgarian company retains ownership of its protected software, artificial intelligence, algorithms, system architecture and integration know-how. The expected partner contribution concerns complementary underwater hardware, manufacturing, physical integration, testing, validation and/or investment supporting market deployment.
technical_problem_evidence_text: The company is seeking partners with expertise in underwater robotics, autonomous or remotely operated underwater vehicles, marine electronics, subsea sensor integration, advanced manufacturing, mechanical and electrical integration, or field validation. Depending on its capabilities, the partner may: •	provide a commercially available open and customisable underwater robotic platform; •	adapt an existing platform for customer-supplied onboard computing and sensors; •	provide sufficient electrical power, payload capacity and thermal management for edge computing; •	provide documented access to telemetry, navigation data, raw sensor data and vehicle interfaces; •	integrate customer-selected sonar, navigation, bathymetric or environmental sensors; •	perform physical, mechanical and electrical integration; •	manufacture prototype mechanical or pressure-resistant components; •	support laboratory, field and pilot validation; •	participate in preparation for commercial deployment; •	or provide strategic investment supporting hardware integration, validation and market entry. The Bulgarian company will retain responsibility for its proprietary software, artificial intelligence, data-processing and system-level integration technology.
title: Bulgarian deep-tech SME seeks partners for integration and validation of an autonomous air-water inspection and mapping technology.

description_text: A Swiss organisation aims to enlarge the offerings of more ethical and sustainable consumer goods. It has created an e-commerce platform which gathers suppliers of climate-neutral and eco-friendly materials, components and parts to offer manufacturers sustainable and eco-responsible alternatives for the production of their products. The Swiss NGO seeks manufacturers, artisans, and factories in Europe or in neighbouring countries also in order to reduce the environmental impact of goods transport producing: • Handbags: all types, from everyday totes to luxury handbags. • Leather goods: wallets, belts, cardholders, and other small accessories. • Watches: including watch straps and cases made from eco-responsible materials. •Travel accessories: luggage tags, passport holders, and travel organizers. • Stationery: notebooks, planners, and pen cases. • Office supplies: desk organizers, document holders, and laptop sleeves. • Home decor: decorative trays, picture frames, and luxury storage boxes. description_text: The Swiss start-up transforms otherwise worthless by-products of the food production to produce cutting-edge eco-friendly alternative-plastic granules, seamlessly tailored for diverse sectors including fashion, outdoor equipment, tools, and toys. Its innovative technology for producing circular, high-quality plastic granulates is based on the use of food by-products as bio-fillers in thermoplastic elastomers (TPE), also known as elastic plastics. A non-exhaustive list of bio-fillers already present in the portfolio are walnuts shells, olive pits, or banana peels. The company already works together with the industry to get hold of the food waste. However, the decentralized availability of food side streams creates difficulties in effectively obtaining relevant resources at large quantities. Therefore, the company seeks further suppliers of food by-products or agriculture waste interested to transform these secondary raw materials into a valuable product. The kind of food by-products the company is interesting in upcycling are: 1. Vegetable oils (e.g. olive oil (waste from oil mills), old frying oil etc.) 2. Shells 3. Fruit pits and stones etc. 4. Second generation feedstock which does not compete with relevant upcycling methods The cooperation could involve developing the necessary supply chain infrastructure and supporting the sourcing of raw materials. Specifically, while the supplier would oversee the sourcing and extraction of feedstock(s) of interest, any required (pre-)treatment processes—such as drying, milling, roasting, or particle coating— could be coordinated jointly, depending on the terms of the agreement. Moreover, the agreement could include the development of extraction processes for suitable waste streams to obtain key building blocks for biopolymer synthesis. For example, this might involve starch extraction from second generation feedstock, contributing to sustainable and resource-efficient operations. The anticipated outcome of this partnership is to establish a consistent, year-round supply of merchandise, with pricing and logistics agreed upon on an annual basis. This approach aims to foster a durable and mutually beneficial collaboration between the parties.

description_text: The company is a Swiss start-up in the materials sector and operates since 2023. It specializes in the synthesis of unique metal-cellulose hybrid fibers. Those can be used for a vast number of applications, one of them being electrical resistance heating. The company focuses on developing their novel heating technology for machine part heating and mobility, and automotive market. In addition, the company is exploring the applicability of their metal-cellulose hybrid fibers in electromagnetic shielding. There, their fibers are compounded with polymers for possible applications in extruded cable shielding jackets or injection molded shielding housings. They could already show the basic manufacturability of their material. Technology and Development: The technology is based on the company’s patent-pending material & synthesis process: natural cellulose fibers are introduced into a wet-chemical synthesis in which metal particles are grown into or onto those fibers. The fibers can stem from any natural source and may be of any length, typically ranging from 0.6 to 2.2 mm mean length. The synthesis takes place in an organic solvent, and the copper source is an organic salt, which is added in powder form. The synthesis allows for tailoring the location and amount of metal particles, therefore also electrical conductivity. For the heating application, those fibers are then further processed into electrically conductive paper and customized with electrodes and packaging to form a heating element, ready for integration. The company has in-house expertise and resources for doing all the mentioned manufacturing in laboratory scale up to 5L volume. In the long run, the company plans to outsource the material synthesis step. Partnership: For the next step in further developing the company’s heating elements, they need to scale the paper manufacturing and customization to pilot plant level. This requires a fiber supply on the kilogram-scale and beyond. In the shielding case, the same holds true. For this scale of synthesis output, the company does not have the infrastructure for, marking the time to start outsourcing their fiber synthesis. The company seeks a partner which is ideally capable of producing the whole range of metal-cellulose fibers. They envision a close collaboration, first starting with an initial pilot phase where the feasibility of further scaling their lab-proven synthesis to a kg-scale  is shown, ensuring product quality and specifications, in the frame of a commercial agreement with technical assistance or R&D collaboration. After successful completion, further scaling steps shall be performed with interest to continue for a longer-term partnership.
technical_problem_evidence_text: The company is seeking a contract manufacturer to outsource the production of its novel material. The ideal partner would offer custom chemical synthesis services on pilot/ commercial scale, while securely handling intellectual property. The material doesn’t require optimization on R&D scale and has been successfully scaled up to 5L in-house. What is still required is the know-how of experienced chemical manufacturers to upscale and produce the material in large volumes. More specifically, the collaboration partner should provide 100L-1000L capacities. The company’s needs include: • For application 1: an output of 200kg per year for 2 years at least. This equals roughly 8 runs of 1000L per year. • For application 2: an output of 30kg until summer 2026. This equals roughly 1 run of 400L. After the completion of the upscaling efforts and the production of the above-mentioned quantities, the company would be interested in a long-term collaboration for commercial production. The production of the metal-cellulose hybrid fibers consists of the wet chemical synthesis and the post processing of the fibers. The multi-addition synthesis involves cellulose fibers, a metal salt in powder form and an organic solvent. The reaction occurs in the range of 140-180°C. The post processing of the fibers involves a washing step with an organic solvent and a size separation method, to remove undesired byproducts. The presence of fibers in the reaction introduces operational and handling challenges. For instance, mixing  in large vessels to ensure successful heat and mass transfer will likely require special consideration. Another technical challenge is the (un)loading of the fibers from the reactor which is conducted manually in house. The product’s quality can be assessed optically, chemically and gravimetrically and could also be done by the company if the partner lacks this equipment. Regarding the cost of the service, the company targets a price at pilot scale production (200 kg/y) on the order of 100 €/kg. The company is aware of the additional costs the initial familiarization and scale-up trials require.
title: Seeking a chemical contract manufacturing partner to scale up and produce at 1000L-scale of metal-cellulose hybrid fibers

description_text: A Swiss luxury jewellery company is developing an innovative additive manufacturing process to produce high-quality 925 sterling silver components using MoldJet technology. The company is actively seeking reliable and scalable alternatives to traditional manufacturing methods, such as investment casting and CNC machining. These conventional processes often result in high scrap rates, limited design flexibility, labour-intensive post-processing, and complex recycling workflows. The company operates in the high-end jewellery segment and focuses on the development of technically demanding and design-driven precious metal components. To expand its production capabilities and improve sustainability, the company aims to validate MoldJet as a near-zero-waste manufacturing process for silver jewellery. This emerging technology is based on the creation of a reusable wax mould that is selectively filled with a metal-containing paste, cured, de-waxed and subsequently sintered to full density. The main objective of the request is to establish a robust and industrially viable MoldJet process chain for 925 sterling silver, covering slurry formulation, printing behaviour, debinding strategy, high-temperature sintering profiles, shrinkage control, porosity reduction and surface quality optimisation. Particular attention is given to dimensional accuracy, surface finish and mechanical performance to meet the stringent requirements of the luxury sector. Representative jewellery components and standard test specimens will be manufactured to validate the process under industrially relevant conditions. The performance of the final parts will be assessed through density measurements, microstructural analysis, hardness testing and dimensional tolerance verification. The results will define the processing window and quality limits of MoldJet for silver. This development supports sustainable production by reducing material losses, enabling wax reuse, decreasing post-processing requirements and improving overall material efficiency. The company is seeking international technology partners with expertise in precious metal pastes, sintering technology, thermal processing or additive manufacturing materials. The targeted collaboration is a research and development cooperation agreement, with the goal of progressing towards industrial implementation and future commercial production.
technical_problem_evidence_text: The partner is expected to contribute advanced technical expertise covering the complete material and thermal processing chain for 925 sterling silver within the MoldJet additive manufacturing route. The collaboration targets the establishment of a fully validated, industrially reliable and reproducible process window suitable for luxury jewellery production. Sintering technology and densification: Expertise in high-temperature sintering of silver alloys, including profile optimisation, shrinkage control, grain growth management and atmosphere selection. The objective is to achieve near-full density (> 99%), minimal residual porosity and high dimensional stability while preserving surface quality suitable for direct jewellery applications. Thermal processing and atmosphere control: Know-how in thermal debinding and sintering under controlled furnace atmospheres (hydrogen, nitrogen, vacuum or mixed environments) to prevent oxidation, contamination and surface degradation. Optimised ramp strategies are required to minimise distortion, blistering and collapse of fine features. Dimensional accuracy and surface finish: Competence in shrinkage modelling, distortion prediction and surface roughness optimisation to reach jewellery-grade surface quality without extensive post-processing. The goal is to enable both functional and aesthetic compliance with luxury sector standards. Quality assurance and material validation: Capability to perform and interpret advanced quality analysis including density (Archimedes, pycnometry), porosity, hardness (Vickers), microstructural analysis (SEM) and dimensional tolerance verification. Both destructive and non-destructive testing approaches are of interest to define stable quality windows. Process maturity and intellectual property protection: The partner must operate at a technology readiness level of at least laboratory-tested or demonstrator stage. All developments must follow IP-safe procedures, ensuring confidentiality and protection of proprietary process knowledge. Exclusions: Technologies based on laser powder bed fusion, PolyJet wax moulding or conventional Binder Jetting systems with high binder content are explicitly excluded from this request, due to their known limitations for silver processing.
title: Process optimisation of 925 Silver for MoldJet additive manufacturing in luxury jewellery

description_text: Founded with the mission to accelerate the transition to a circular economy, a Swiss startup specializing in sustainable industrial chemistry and eco-friendly additive development leverages advanced material science to transform industrial waste streams into valuable manufacturing inputs. Operating with a lean structure and cutting-edge vision, the organization focuses on developing scalable, green chemical solutions that mitigate the environmental footprint of traditional manufacturing materials. The company seeks manufacturers of rubber goods or industrial organization to co-develop and scale up rubber recycling through a more sustainable devulcanization process. The global vulcanized rubber industry faces a severe waste management challenge. Traditional vulcanization creates permanent, crosslinked sulfur bonds within the rubber matrix. These bonds make the material durable but also difficult to recycle. Standard mechanical grinding merely downgrades the material into low-value filler, while incineration and landfilling create significant environmental liabilities. To solve this problem, the startup offers a high-performance eco-friendly chemical additive for rubber devulcanization. The product functions via a gentle chemical-mechanical process that targets and breaks down the sulfur-sulfur crosslinks while preserving the integrity of the main polymer chains. The resulting material acts as a functional secondary raw material that retains the inherent elastomeric or abrasion properties of the original feedstock. While not all recovered rubber is highly formulated, preserving the original compound's existing additives in highly compounded inputs - like tires - allows manufacturers to optimize formulations and reduce the volume of new chemical inputs. While the chemical formulation is available, the core problem to be solved lies in its end-user application. The startup requires advanced end-user technical manufacturing know-how and material testing capabilities. Specifically, the technology requested involves the practical application, compounding, and performance validation of the devulcanized material when it is blended back into new product lines. Collaboration with manufacturers of technical rubber goods, consumer rubber products or industrial organization seeking sustainable technologies to recycle their rubber waste would allow to determine how the treated rubber behaves during industrial molding and production, ensuring it seamlessly integrates into new technical rubber goods or consumer products without compromising final structural integrity. Transitioning a chemical formulation into a successful, commercial-grade end product requires a collaborative feedback loop between the chemical developer and the material manufacturer. Technical cooperation or joint venture with manufacturers of technical rubber goods, consumer rubber products or industrial organization is thought: to co-develop optimized blending guidelines and successful manufacture market-ready consumer or technical rubber goods containing high percentages of recycled material. Unlike conventional high-temperature devulcanization methods, our chemical-mechanical process operates efficiently under reduced thermal requirements without demanding high-heat inputs, lowering energy consumption. By providing a substitute for resource-intensive virgin materials, this method inherently drives a substantial reduction in the overall process carbon footprint. Cooperation throught: commercial agreements, or joint development projects (Eurostars or Horizon Europe) if mutually beneficial. Partners are expected to provide industrial testing environments, product compounding expertise, and quality assurance evaluation for the final rubber products. The start up is also open to joint venture or partnership that support both the validation of the innovation and the integration of recycled  rubber materials into new goods or consumer products.
technical_problem_evidence_text: Performance, Ease of Use, and Quality Required The startup offers a high-performance chemical additive that transforms scrap rubber into a reusable asset. We require technical partners to test the product and evaluate the devulcanized material to optimize blending ratios within their product lines. The primary technical objective is verifying how the material behaves during industrial molding and production, ensuring it integrates into new technical rubber goods or consumer products without compromising final mechanical properties. Capability and Equipment Requirements End-user partners must have operational facilities utilizing conventional, standard rubber processing equipment (such as standard extruders, open mills, or internal mixers). The partner must possess internal material testing capabilities, compound formulation expertise, and final product quality validation workflows. The partner will be responsible for evaluating the mechanical tolerances, durability, and dimensional stability of the final rubber products containing the recycled material. Sustainability and Compliance Standards Because the additive and its supply chains are fully compliant with the European Union Regulation on Deforestation-free Products (EUDR), partners must be capable of maintaining matching environmental tracking and quality assurance standards throughout their compounding trials. Sustainability and Compliance Standards A key environmental capability of this process is that the resulting recycled rubber produced by the partner can fully comply with the European Union Regulation on Deforestation-free Products (EUDR). While not strictly mandatory for initial testing, it would be an advantage if partners possess the quality assurance tracking and environmental standards necessary to maintain this regulatory compliance throughout their compounding and manufacturing trials. Stage of Development Needed Partners at the prototype, pilot, or commercial stage are welcome. Ideally, the partner has the flexibility to perform pilot-scale compounding runs or help translate initial test results into commercial-grade production logic, though we are open to discussing different scales of cooperation. The ideal partner is an end-user manufacturer or sustainability-driven organization looking to test the startup's chemical additive within standard rubber processing setups to achieve devulcanization. They will collaborate with the startup to evaluate how the additive integrates, optimize compounding mixtures for their specific products, and provide feedback on the final product's performance.
title: Manufacturers of rubber products sought for co-development of sustainable and circular devulcanization of waste materials

description_text: A Swiss organisation linked to the Geneva Forum and the Geneva Foundation for the Future is seeking user organisations worldwide to test, use and deploy the impact finance evaluation framework AGILE within real decision-making processes. technical_problem_evidence_text: The goal is to develop an effervescent tablet with protein as the main component. The choice of raw materials and production processes must also account for product cost-efficiency. Specifications: • Protein per tablet: Minimum 12g • Tablet size: 32 mm diameter (custom size) • Dissolution behavior: Full, clear, residue-free dissolution in <2 minutes in 200–300 ml of water • Solution appearance: Clear, no sediment, pleasant sensory profile (taste, smell, color) • Stability: Tablets must remain stable in form and suitable for storage • Powder flowability: Must be suitable for machine-based tablet production • Food-safe additives only: Must comply with EU food regulations • No compromises on food safety and hygiene (HACCP, GMP compliant)

description_text: The applicant is a German SME operating in structured content production and multi-format publishing. Over the last four years the company has developed a semantic anchoring system that gives every relevant text element in an editable office-format document a persistent identifier. References stay attached to their content when documents are restructured, edited under change tracking or export-ed to several output channels in parallel. Per document the system handles between 3,000 and 9,000 anchored references. The system has been in productive use in the company's own editorial domain since late 2024. The intended cooperation moves the technology into a different field: regulated technical documentation for medical devices under MDR 2017/745. References in that field are not editorial. A symbol, a warning, a product identifier or a clinical claim carries regulatory weight, and it has to stay consistent through the whole product life cycle, through up to 24 language versions, and through every audit a Notified Body decides to run. Tools used today in this market rely either on rigid component content management, on manual reference maintenance, or on layout workflows that lose semantic links somewhere between a translation round and a release approval. The company has seen no toolchain that solves this without trade-offs. The project builds on the existing anchoring technology but requires substantial experimental development. Unresolved technical challenges concern the preservation of regulatory meaning across structural edits, multilingual transformations, terminology changes, redlining and controlled release processes. On top of this sit integration with translation memory and controlled terminology; audit trails that satisfy ISO 13485 change-control duties and MDR Annex II documentation requirements; mechanisms that carry the regulatory weight of a reference through translation, redlining and release; and validation methods that generate evidence suitable for review during quality-management and conformity-assessment audits. The cooperation delivers a demonstrator validated against real cases from the partner, plus an evaluation framework for regulatory fit. The cooperation is designed for the German ZIM cooperative project track. Each side runs its own work packages and holds its own grant share. The company brings running technology, software-side R&D capacity and document-structure expertise. The partner brings the regulated domain and contributes its own regulatory-methodological R&D work packages — among them the development of a formal regulatory reference model, risk-based validation criteria, multilingual compliance rules, and methods for verifying reference integrity across document revisions, translations and release processes. The parties intend to conclude a research and development cooperation agreement for the planned project. Rights to pre-existing technology, jointly developed results and subsequent exploitation will be regulated in a project-specific cooperation agreement.
technical_problem_evidence_text: Sought is a partner with operational responsibility for MDR-regulated documentation. The partner brings the regulated domain the applicant does not have in-house. description_text: The Danish SME develops reusable container solutions for catering and takeaway with the objective of reducing single‑use packaging and improving circular return systems. To support efficient return logistics, the company is seeking a technology capable of reliable single‑item identification of reusable food containers (e.g. bowls, plates, trays). The containers are manufactured from a wood‑plastic composite (WPC) material and are designed for repeated reuse under demanding operational conditions. They must withstand industrial dishwashing, microwave heating, oven exposure and freezing without degradation. Any identification solution must tolerate the same conditions over the product lifetime. The purpose of the identification technology is to enable operational tracking and identification during use and return cycles (e.g. in catering kitchens and return facilities). The solution is not consumer‑facing and does not require anti‑counterfeiting or brand protection features. A key operational requirement is that containers cannot be guaranteed a fixed orientation during scanning. The requested technology must therefore be orientation‑independent, either through surface‑wide identification or through identification principles that do not rely on a predefined code position. Containers are scanned in two main environments: Small‑scale or decentralised operations using standard smartphones High‑volume kitchens using fixed or tunnel‑mounted industrial camera systems The company is not seeking a full end‑to‑end tracking platform, but rather access to the core identification technology (e.g. algorithm, SDK (Software Development Kit), or licensable method) that can be integrated into its own backend systems. Material‑intrinsic identification The container material has a naturally heterogeneous surface structure, with visible wood fibres distributed randomly. This inherent variability means that no two containers are identical, opening the possibility of identification based on the material itself. Solutions based on surface fingerprinting or material‑intrinsic identification, where the natural surface structure is captured (e.g. optically) and used as a unique identifier are therefore of strong interest, provided they can reliably identify individual containers over the full product lifetime despite normal wear and cleaning.
technical_problem_evidence_text: The requested technology should meet the following requirements: -Enables single‑item identification (each container uniquely identifiable) -Implemented as: integrated surface marking (e.g. engraving or sandblasting), or material‑intrinsic identification (e.g. surface fingerprinting) (adhesive labels and add‑on tags are out of scope) -Readable using standard smartphones and industrial camera systems -Orientation‑independent reading -Withstands: industrial dishwashing (~85 °C) microwave use (up to 1000 W) freezing (−18 °C) oven exposure up to 135 °C for at least 35 minutes -Minimum 200+ reuse cycles without loss of identification reliability -Compatible with wood‑plastic composite (WPC) materials -No dependency on proprietary platforms, closed ecosystems or mandatory cloud services -Available as a technology licence or core technology access (SDK, library, algorithm, or equivalent) -Cost structure suitable for SME‑scale deployment (initial volumes approx. 5,000–50,000 units/year) Solutions leveraging the material’s natural surface variation as identifier (e.g. surface fingerprinting) are equally welcome.
title: Single‑Item Identification for Reusable Food Containers Using Surface‑Based Technologies sought by Danish SME

description_text: A French company founded 40 years ago, designs electron accelerators whose properties enable applications in the fields of cables and wires, rubber and heat-shrinkable electrical components. description_text: A French SME active in the circular economy and the refurbishment of bicycles has developed secondo.bike, a B2B marketplace enabling professional users (repair workshops, fleet operators, associations, manufacturers) to exchange and purchase refurbished or dormant spare parts. While the marketplace is operational, adoption is slowed by a structural barrier: spare parts typically have a low unit value, making manual listing (photography, measurements, detailed descriptions, compatibility information) too time-consuming for most professional users. To address this challenge and scale up reuse practices, the company is initiating the development of a shared technological foundation based on artificial intelligence and computer vision. The objective is to enable users to identify a component from a single photo, retrieve structured data from dedicated product databases, and automatically create a pre-filled listing suitable for circular marketplaces such as secondo.bike. The problem addressed is not specific to the bicycle industry. Similar constraints exist in many sectors: home appliances, power tools, machinery, electronic equipment and more. In these fields, the ability to reliably identify a component and source a replacement — whether new or reused — is a prerequisite for repairing and extending product life. The envisaged technological platform would include: ●	domain-specific databases of components and product structures, ●	AI-based image recognition and similarity search, ●	automated generation of structured product listings, ●	optional diagnostic support tools, ●	mechanisms enabling manufacturers to provide official component images and data to improve recognition accuracy. By co-developing this technological layer with international partners, the project aims to support large-scale reuse, improve product repairability, and offer manufacturers a pathway toward “repair-ready” labelling frameworks.
technical_problem_evidence_text: The company seeks international partners for R&D collaboration to co-design and train recognition models, enrich databases, and test the tools in multiple industrial domains. Commercial agreements with technical assistance may also be envisaged for partners integrating the technology into existing digital platforms. Investment partnerships may be relevant for scaling the solution globally.
title: AI-enabled component recognition and automated listing technology to support circular marketplaces and the reuse of spare parts

description_text: The French research institute has extensive expertise in infant electroencephalogram recordings using high-density nets with 128 and 252 electrodes in babies as young as a few months old. These systems have enabled major advances in the study of early cognitive and brain development, yet they also expose significant technological limitations. This is precisely why the institute is seeking research and development cooperation agreements to overcome these challenges and drive innovation. The primary objective is to further increase spatial sampling by developing a new high-density EEG cap with approximately 280 electrodes , specifically designed for infants and fully compatible with the BEL/EGI EEG acquisition system. In infants, the low conductivity and thickness of the skull strongly reduce the spatial smearing observed in adults, making ultra-high-density EEG particularly informative. Increasing electrode density therefore has a high potential payoff in terms of spatial resolution, source localization, and network analyses in early development. A second major challenge concerns signal quality. While dry electrodes are essential for fast and well-tolerated recordings in young infants, their signal-to-noise ratio is not always optimal, especially for cognitive paradigms requiring fine temporal and spatial precision. The French institute is therefore seeking to develop or integrate an improved dry-electrode technology that offers better and more stable contact, reduced impedance, and higher SNR, while preserving the key practical advantages of current EGI systems. The cap must be extremely fast to install, comfortable, and safe for very young infants, minimizing stress, movement, and preparation time. These constraints are critical for successful data acquisition in both research and clinical contexts. The resulting system should be robust enough for longitudinal studies and scalable to large cohorts. This technology will directly support cutting-edge cognitive neuroscience studies of early brain development and learning, and will also enable clinical translation by improving the reliability of EEG-based biomarkers for neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs). Ultimately, this project aims to push infant EEG beyond current limits by combining ultra-high spatial density, excellent signal quality, and real-world usability.
technical_problem_evidence_text: Expertise in the design and fabrication of ultra-high-density EEG electrodes and caps for scalp recordings, including advanced dry-electrode materials inspired by intracranial technologies (e.g. conductive polymers, nano-textured surfaces). Experience with low-impedance, high-SNR electrodes, active electronics, rapid-mount systems, and mechanical designs ensuring comfort and stability in infants.
title: High-density electroencephalogram (EEG) for babies

description_text: The company is building a new infrastructure layer for the impact economy, addressing one of the biggest gaps in sustainability today: the lack of verifiable, trustworthy and auditable impact data. Current ESG reporting is fragmented, declarative and difficult to validate. Organizations struggle to demonstrate that their actions generate real, measurable outcomes, creating a critical trust gap between companies, institutions and stakeholders. The company addresses this challenge by transforming real-world problems into structured, traceable and verifiable impact through a unified system. At the core of this system is Impact Graph, a structured workflow engine that enables organizations to transform ideas, decisions, projects or initiatives into verifiable processes. It supports: - the decomposition of actions into structured workflows - the attachment of real evidence (documents, links, files) - the generation of structured records - the creation of traceable timelines - the preparation of projects for external verification This approach turns intention into structured evidence. The platform combines : - A discovery layer where ideas, initiatives and projects emerge and are validated by the community - Impact Graph for structuring workflows and preparing projects for verification and funding - AI-driven analysis to guide decisions and execution - A traceability layer to record decisions, processes and evidence - A data integrity layer ensuring structured and verifiable information - A blockchain anchoring layer securing checkpoints and proofs - Proof-of-Impact mechanisms to certify and validate real-world outcomes Together, these components create a complete system in which every step—from problem identification to funding readiness—is structured, traceable and verifiable. This enables a new flow : problem → solution → initiative → structured workflow → evidence → verification → funding readiness The system is designed as a distributed infrastructure capable of operating locally (including in offline environments) and synchronizing with global networks. This architecture enables deployment across sectors such as energy, manufacturing, smart buildings, healthcare and sustainable infrastructure. Use cases include: - Impact measurement and certification for ESG and sustainability programs - Structuring projects to access grants and funding - Community-driven initiatives and crowdfunding with verifiable outcomes - Operational traceability in industrial environments - Energy monitoring and optimization - Transparent reporting for institutions, corporates and public-sector actors By bridging the gap between real-world actions and digital verification, the company enables organizations to move from declarative ESG reporting to measurable, auditable and trusted impact. The long-term vision is to establish Proof‑of‑Impact as a global standard for how impact is structured, verified and trusted. The company aims to provide a system that structures, verifies and certifies impact from end to end.
technical_problem_evidence_text: The company is seeking technical and strategic partners in the following areas: - industrial and energy infrastructure (smart grids, buildings, industrial sites) - IoT, edge computing and embedded systems - cybersecurity, data integrity and blockchain infrastructure - ESG, impact measurement and certification frameworks - AI and data analytics applied to real‑world operations The objective is to co‑develop, pilot and scale the infrastructure in real‑world environments, accelerating adoption across sectors and geographies. The french company is developing a distributed infrastructure for verifiable impact, combining AI, structured traceability systems and cryptographic integrity layers. The system is built on a modular architecture that includes: - an AI‑driven operational layer for event interpretation, decision support and automation - a traceability system capturing actions, decisions, evidence and impact signals - a data integrity and anchoring layer ensuring reliability and verification - Proof‑of‑Impact mechanisms enabling certification and validation of real‑world outcomes - Impact Graph for workflow structuring and evidence preparation The project is supported by proprietary intellectual property currently under development, including: - a patent on the transmission of signed metadata via power line communication (PLC), enabling secure data exchange through energy infrastructure - a patent on the integration of energy equipment as physical nodes of the system, supporting distributed validation and edge‑level data collection - a registered utility model related to the Proof‑of‑Impact methodology These innovations enable a hybrid infrastructure that bridges digital systems and physical environments, designed for deployment in industrial, energy and infrastructure contexts.

description_text: In the metal recycling sector in which the SME operates, the company produces non-ferrous materials with varying compositions. description_text: Founded in 1985, a French industrial confectionery company (employing 190 staff) active in the production of bubble gum and related products is facing challenges related to the management of its bubble gum paste waste generated during the manufacturing process. This waste is produced in the form of compact blocks weighing several dozen kilograms and is currently treated as general industrial waste. It contains elastomers and resins, giving it a highly elastic and non-brittle structure. The material can become hard externally while remaining malleable internally. It softens when heated and cannot be crushed unless cooled below freezing. Due to its composition, traditional waste management methods such as incineration or anaerobic digestion are not suitable. The company is therefore seeking a technical solution capable of processing this material in order to improve recycling efficiency and reduce environmental impact. The objective is to identify a solution that is technically feasible, economically viable, and compliant with European regulations. Implementation is foreseen at two industrial sites, located approximately 300 km apart. The company is specifically interested in a commercial agreement with technical assistance, allowing the integration of the proposed technology into its industrial processes. The expected outcome is the deployment of a sustainable and economically viable recycling solution.

description_text: Invasive underwater aquatic plants, such as water crassula and large water primrose, are an increasing problem in the Netherlands. These plants spread rapidly and suffocate native flora and fauna, leading to a significant decline in biodiversity. Additionally, they obstruct water flow in ditches and canals, which can result in flooding. Recreational activities, such as boating and fishing, are also negatively affected as waterways become inaccessible. The traditional approach to managing invasive aquatic plants mainly involves physical removal and maintenance. This is done using mowing boats to cut and remove the plants. In some cases, manual methods, such as pulling out plants by hand, are used by volunteers. Additionally, ditches and canals are dredged more frequently to remove seeds and root fragments. While these methods are effective in the short term, they require repeated efforts and ongoing monitoring to prevent regrowth. Early detection of invasive species is crucial to contain their spread and prevent large-scale damage to ecosystems, water management, and recreation. Identifying these plants in the early stages allows for targeted and cost-effective management measures, saving time and resources. Additionally, it helps prevent invasive species from displacing native flora and fauna or completely obstructing waterways. Early detection in Dutch waters is challenging due to several factors: 1.	Extensive and diverse water system: The Netherlands has a dense network of ditches, canals, lakes, and ponds, making it a massive challenge to monitor all water bodies effectively. 2.	Visual similarity to native species: Many invasive plants closely resemble native aquatic plants, making identification difficult without specialized knowledge or technology. 3.	Rapid spread: Due to water currents, boats, and human activity, invasive species can spread quickly, complicating efforts to locate and contain outbreaks. 4. Plants must be identified while spreading on the bottom / the water "floor" before the plants come to the surface. That is why it needs to work in murky waters. 5	Limited visibility: Many invasive plants grow underwater or in murky conditions, which hinders visual detection.

description_text: Based in the Netherlands, the research institute focuses on neuromorphic computing, a new computing paradigm inspired by the way the brain works. The institute, affiliated with a large public university, brings together expertise from multiple domains, including mathematics, physics, materials science, computer science, artificial intelligence, electrical engineering, and robotics. The team works across all levels of the technological stack, from materials and components to chips, algorithms, and applications. Neuromorphic computing represents a novel approach to both hardware and algorithms, applying principles derived from brain functionality to achieve highly efficient computational systems. The institute aims to build systems that apply one or more brain-inspired mechanisms that make biological cognition remarkably efficient. The human brain’s efficiency, estimated to be up to 10,000 times greater than current computing systems, arises from several core principles. For instance, the brain processes information in a massively parallel manner, enabled by the dense interconnection of neurons (through synapses) and the close integration of memory and computation. These characteristics allow for substantial reductions in energy consumption. As an emerging field, neuromorphic computing requires collaboration across various technological layers — from materials and chip design to algorithms and real-world applications — to transition from laboratory concepts to practical use. The research centre is seeking partners who can contribute to this ambition through collaboration in a pre-competitive research setting. Specifically, the institute is interested in working with partners who can provide: •	Specific technologies, such as sensors, low-power electronics, edge computing solutions, or embedded artificial intelligence; •	Practical use cases in sectors such as health, mobility, sensing, or infrastructure, where local, adaptive computing could deliver tangible impact. The objective is to jointly explore, design, and validate neuromorphic technologies, demonstrating their feasibility in real applications while integrating end-user requirements early in the design process.

description_text: This Dutch deep-tech SME is active in the field of quantum technology and structural health monitoring, and is developing a patented surface coating that can turn everyday structures such as aircraft, bridges, wind turbines, ships and industrial equipment into continuous, contactless sensors. The technology requested is access to a laboratory with an operational setup for a specialised optical-magnetic measurement technique used to characterise microscopic defects in diamond material. This know-how and equipment is needed because the company has completed an extensive computational modelling programme, using five independent simulation tools across 22 separate studies, and the final missing step before physical proof-of-concept is a single, clearly defined laboratory measurement on coated diamond plate samples that the company will supply, together with a measurement protocol. Specifically, the technique requested is optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) on nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centres in diamond. The coating is diamond-based and is sensitive, at a quantum level, to temperature, mechanical strain and magnetic fields. This information can be read out simply by illuminating the surface with light — remotely and without any physical contact. In this way, the entire coated surface becomes a sensor, without the need for wiring or embedded electronics, allowing early detection of micro-damage long before it would be visible through conventional inspection. Compared with conventional structural health monitoring — discrete, wired sensors that each measure a single parameter at fixed points — the coating measures temperature, strain and magnetic fields simultaneously, across the entire coated surface. To the company's knowledge, no current player combines quantum-grade sensing with a deployable structural coating. The desired outcome of an international partnership is to obtain independent, credible experimental confirmation that the coating performs as the simulations predict, which would allow the company to move toward licensing the technology to European industrial partners in aerospace, coatings and infrastructure monitoring. International cooperation is envisaged as a short, clearly scoped project of about six to twelve weeks, carried out under a non-disclosure agreement, with samples and a measurement protocol provided by the requesting company, and with the possibility of a longer-term joint research project, for example under a European research funding programme, should the initial validation succeed.
technical_problem_evidence_text: Required: an operational ODMR setup for NV-centre characterisation — 532 nm excitation, microwave control around 2.87 GHz, fluorescence detection (confocal or wide-field); ability to measure macroscopic coated plate samples. CW-ODMR is required; Pulsed ODMR (Ramsey / spin-echo) is a plus; temperature- and strain-dependent measurement capability is desirable. Practical: capacity to start within weeks, willingness to work under NDA; samples and measurement protocol will be supplied by the Dutch company.
title: Dutch diamond R&D company, active in the field of quantum sensing, seeks a measurement laboratory partner to validate a diamond-based coating for monitoring the structural health of critical infrastructure.

description_text: Background Biomethane injected into the natural gas grid must comply with strict gas quality specifications. One of these requirements is that the gas must have the same odor characteristics as natural gas, which is achieved through the addition of an odorant. During biomethane production, Volatile Organic Compounds (VOC) can occasionally be present in the gas stream. These compounds may mask the odorant, resulting in reduced odor perception and potentially causing the biomethane to fail grid injection requirements. To prevent this issue, Volatile Organic Compounds are typically removed using activated carbon filtration systems. However, it is often difficult to determine when an activated carbon filter is approaching saturation. As a result, Volatile Organic Compounds breakthrough can occur before filter replacement is initiated. Technical Challenge We are seeking a monitoring solution capable of detecting or predicting the breakthrough of volatile fatty acids in activated carbon filters used in biomethane production facilities. The ideal system should: Continuously or periodically monitor the gas stream downstream of the activated carbon filter. Detect the presence of volatile fatty acids at very low concentrations before they reach levels that can interfere with odor perception. Provide early warning of impending filter saturation or breakthrough. Operate reliably in biomethane production environments. Be suitable for integration into existing gas treatment installations. Expected Outcome The objective is to develop a reliable method for determining the optimal replacement moment of activated carbon filters, thereby preventing Volatile Organic Compounds breakthrough, ensuring compliance with biomethane grid injection specifications, and reducing unnecessary filter replacement costs.
technical_problem_evidence_text: The client would like to identify technology providers, research organizations, or industrial partners that can offer: Existing commercial solutions for VOC breakthrough monitoring. Sensor technologies capable of detecting Volatile Organic Compounds in biomethane streams. Online analytical instruments or monitoring systems. Innovative methods for predicting activated carbon saturation and optimizing filter replacement intervals. Expertise in gas quality monitoring for biomethane and renewable gas applications. Type of Cooperation Sought Commercial agreement with technical assistance Technical cooperation agreement Research and development cooperation Pilot or demonstration projects
title: Innovative monitoring solutions and sensor technologies sought to prevent Volatile Organic Compounds (VOC) breakthrough in biomethane streams
